task: iTantra PS-26173 device-tier model decision: monolingual 120M vs multilingual 628M

dataset.name: google/fleurs test split (local pinned copy)
dataset.selection: manifest.csv rows for the language, sorted by audio_path, first N (deterministic)
dataset.note: Read speech. Kathbath/IndicVoices audio is not present in this project, so FLEURS was used.

normalization: Unicode NFC, casefold (lowercase), every Unicode punctuation (P*) and symbol (S*) character replaced with a space, then whitespace collapsed and stripped. Indic combining marks are preserved. WER computed with jiwer.wer() on whitespace-separated tokens of the normalized strings.

metrics.WER: percent, jiwer.wer() over normalized whitespace tokens, corpus-level
metrics.RTF: sum(per-sample inference seconds) / sum(audio seconds); excludes model load and audio decode
metrics.peak_RAM_MB: peak process RSS sampled at 50 ms across model load + inference, one model per process
metrics.disk_MB: on-disk size of the weights actually loaded

caveats: RTF is not a pure architecture comparison: the multilingual model runs as ONNX Runtime graphs (operator-fused, release-optimized) while the monolingual model runs as eager PyTorch/NeMo. WER is unaffected by this; RTF favours the multilingual runtime.
Decoders differ: multilingual is CTC with a per-language vocabulary mask (the only path this project ships); the monolingual hybrid is decoded with its own head.
CPU-only, 4 threads, to approximate phone-class compute rather than the dev GPU.
